Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("wallpaper32.exe","wallpaper64.exe") AND (Processes.process_name IN ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","mshta.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","Synaptics.exe") OR Processes.process IN ("*\\._cache_*.exe","*\\AppData\\Local\\Temp\\*","*\\AppData\\Roaming\\*","*\\ProgramData\\*")) by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.parent_process_name Processes.process_name Processes.process Processes.process_path | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | `security_content_ctime(firstTime)` | `security_content_ctime(lastTime)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("wallpaper32.exe","wallpaper64.exe") AND (Processes.process_name IN ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","mshta.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","Synaptics.exe") OR Processes.process IN ("*\\._cache_*.exe","*\\AppData\\Local\\Temp\\*","*\\AppData\\Roaming\\*","*\\ProgramData\\*")) by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.parent_process_name Processes.process_name Processes.process Processes.process_path | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | `security_content_ctime(firstTime)` | `security_content_ctime(lastTime)`
Campaign loader '._cache_GAME1.exe' execution (Steam wallpaper malware) AIInstallation High
Alerts on execution of the campaign's loader module whose filename begins with the distinctive '._cache_' prefix (e.g. ._cache_GAME1.exe). This module boots the decoy game NTRaholic while simultaneously sideloading the tampered AggregatorHost.dll Steam credential stealer. Rationale: The '._cache_GAME1.exe' string is a verbatim, highly distinctive code-block IOC from the article — the leading dot-underscore prefix is unusual enough on Windows that the prefix match alone is near-zero FP and double-confirmed by second-source write-ups. Cross-checked against: • https://securelist.com/dozens-of-malicious-wallpapers-found-on-steam-workshop/120186/ • https://cybersecuritynews.com/steam-workshop-abused/ • https://www.technadu.com/malicious-steam-workshop-wallpapers-hijack-accounts-via-wallpaper-engine-distribute-darkkomet-lumma-vidar-and-renengine/629591/
ATT&CKT1204.002 T1574.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • A benign application that legitimately uses a '._cache_'-prefixed temp executable naming convention (rare)
  • Security tooling re-detonating the sample in a sandbox on a monitored host
  • Backup/restore of a previously infected user profile re-surfacing the artifact
Response runbook
1) Triage: capture the SHA256/MD5 and folder path of the ._cache_ process and its parent (expect a wallpaper package dir); confirm against the article hash set. 2) Contain: isolate the host, kill the process, and quarantine the parent wallpaper directory; block the hash org-wide. 3) Hunt: search the same host and others for AggregatorHost.dll image loads, Synaptics.exe drops in ProgramData, and C2 to 120.48.156.17/ey.php.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(14d)
| where FileName startswith "._cache_"
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, FolderPath, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessFolderPath, SHA256, MD5
| order by Timestamp desc
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(14d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where NewProcessName has @"\._cache_"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, SubjectUserName, ParentProcessName, NewProcessName, CommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc

DarkKomet Synaptics.exe backdoor executing from ProgramData AIInstallation High
Alerts when a process named Synaptics.exe runs from C:\ProgramData\Synaptics\ — the DarkKomet backdoor masquerading as the Synaptics touchpad driver, dropped by the malicious wallpaper. The legitimate Synaptics driver runs from Program Files / DriverStore, never from ProgramData\Synaptics, making the path a clean discriminator. Rationale: Second sources (Trend Micro DarkKomet encyclopedia, CyberSecurityNews) confirm the backdoor drops to C:\ProgramData\Synaptics\Synaptics.exe under the 'Synaptics Pointing Device Driver' guise; the ProgramData\Synaptics path is the discriminator that separates malware from the genuine driver. Cross-checked against: • https://securelist.com/dozens-of-malicious-wallpapers-found-on-steam-workshop/120186/ • https://cybersecuritynews.com/steam-workshop-abused/ • https://www.trendmicro.com/vinfo/us/threat-encyclopedia/malware/backdoor.msil.darkkomet.ac

  • Security sandbox detonating the sample on a monitored host
Response runbook
1) Triage: confirm the binary's signature (DarkKomet is unsigned or fake-signed) and hash against the campaign IOC set; check the parent process for a wallpaper/loader origin. 2) Contain: isolate the host, kill Synaptics.exe, and delete the C:\ProgramData\Synaptics directory and its Run-key persistence value. 3) Hunt: look for the 'Synaptics Pointing Device Driver' Run value pointing to ProgramData, AggregatorHost.dll loads, and DarkKomet C2 beacons.

Tampered AggregatorHost.dll loaded/dropped (Steam session credential theft) AIActions on Objectives High
Hunts for the malicious AggregatorHost.dll — a tampered system-library name sideloaded by ._cache_GAME1.exe to locate the Steam client and hijack the live session. Windows ships AggregatorHost.exe, not a DLL by this name, so any AggregatorHost.dll outside System32/SysWOW64 is anomalous. Rationale: AggregatorHost.dll is named verbatim in the article and confirmed by second sources as the patched library that hunts the Steam client and hijacks the session; keying on the DLL name plus a System32/SysWOW64 exclusion makes any hit high-fidelity. Cross-checked against: • https://securelist.com/dozens-of-malicious-wallpapers-found-on-steam-workshop/120186/ • https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/security/steam-workshop-abused-to-spread-malware-via-wallpaper-engine-app/ • https://cybersecuritynews.com/steam-workshop-abused/

Response runbook
1) Triage: identify the loading process (expect ._cache_GAME1.exe or a wallpaper binary) and hash the DLL; confirm the host has the Steam client and an active session. 2) Contain: isolate the host, terminate the loader, quarantine the DLL, and force a Steam credential/session reset for the user (revoke active sessions, change password). 3) Hunt: pivot to outbound traffic to 120.48.156.17/ey.php, Synaptics.exe persistence, and any other hosts loading AggregatorHost.dll from non-system paths.

C2 communication to Steam wallpaper campaign infrastructure (120.48.156.17 / 202.144.192.29) AICommand & Control Medium
Alerts on any host connecting to the campaign's confirmed C2 IPs or the specific exfil/download URLs (ey.php, audit.php, download2/Themes2.zip). AggregatorHost.dll posts stolen Steam session data to 120.48.156.17/ey.php; 202.144.192.29 serves second-stage payloads. Rationale: 120.48.156.17/ey.php is a verbatim code-block IOC and 202.144.192.29 (with audit.php and download2/Themes2.zip) is in the article's IOC list; both confirmed across second-source write-ups. Hardcoded IP/URL matches are inherently low-FP. Cross-checked against: • https://securelist.com/dozens-of-malicious-wallpapers-found-on-steam-workshop/120186/ • https://cybersecuritynews.com/steam-workshop-abused/ • https://www.technadu.com/malicious-steam-workshop-wallpapers-hijack-accounts-via-wallpaper-engine-distribute-darkkomet-lumma-vidar-and-renengine/629591/

Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Threat-intel scanner or security analyst sandbox deliberately reaching the IOC
  • Proxy/IDS replaying or validating the indicator
  • Shared-hosting IP reuse where a benign service later occupies the address (re-validate IOC freshness)
Response runbook
1) Triage: identify the initiating process (expect AggregatorHost.dll host, Synaptics.exe, or a wallpaper binary) and the bytes/direction of the flow to gauge exfil vs download. 2) Contain: block both IPs at the perimeter, isolate the host, and reset/revoke the user's Steam session and password. 3) Hunt: sweep all hosts for these IPs over 90 days, then pivot on each hit to AggregatorHost.dll loads and Synaptics.exe persistence.

| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessFolderPath, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, RemoteIP, RemotePort, RemoteUrl, Protocol
| order by Timestamp desc

DarkKomet 'Synaptics Pointing Device Driver' Run-key persistence to ProgramData AIInstallation High
Alerts when a CurrentVersion\Run value (commonly named 'Synaptics Pointing Device Driver') is set with data pointing to C:\ProgramData\Synaptics\Synaptics.exe. The malware reuses the genuine driver's value name but redirects it to ProgramData, so the value DATA path is the discriminator from the legitimate Program Files entry. Rationale: Second sources document the exact persistence: a Run value 'Synaptics Pointing Device Driver' redirected to C:\ProgramData\Synaptics\Synaptics.exe. Matching the value DATA path (ProgramData\Synaptics) avoids FPs from the legitimate driver, which targets Program Files. Datadog left empty: the provided Sysmon schema exposes @TargetObject (the key/value name) but not the value DATA, and the value name alone matches the genuine driver — so a clean Datadog expression isn't possible on this tenant's fields. Cross-checked against: • https://securelist.com/dozens-of-malicious-wallpapers-found-on-steam-workshop/120186/ • https://cybersecuritynews.com/steam-workshop-abused/ • https://www.trendmicro.com/vinfo/us/threat-encyclopedia/malware/backdoor.msil.darkkomet.ac

Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment

  • Profile/image restore re-applying a previously planted Run value
  • Security sandbox detonation on a monitored host
Response runbook
1) Triage: confirm the Run value DATA resolves to ProgramData\Synaptics\Synaptics.exe and the target binary is unsigned/matches campaign hashes; note the writing process. 2) Contain: isolate the host, delete the Run value and the ProgramData\Synaptics directory, and terminate any running Synaptics.exe. 3) Hunt: enumerate other hosts for the same Run-value data, AggregatorHost.dll loads, and C2 to 120.48.156.17.

| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where ActionType in ("RegistryValueSet","RegistryKeyCreated")
| where RegistryKey has @"\CurrentVersion\Run"
| where RegistryValueData has @"\ProgramData\Synaptics\Synaptics.exe"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessFolderPath, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, RegistryKey, RegistryValueName, RegistryValueData
| order by Timestamp desc
ImRegistryEvent

| order by TimeGenerated desc

Steam wallpaper campaign payload hash sweep (DarkKomet / Lumma / Vidar / RenEngine) AIDelivery Medium
Retrospective and forward IOC sweep for the 13 MD5 hashes published for this campaign across process executions and file writes. Catches any campaign payload variant (DarkKomet backdoor, Lumma/Vidar stealers, RenEngine downloader, miners) regardless of filename or delivery packaging. Rationale: Uses the 13 published MD5 IOCs verbatim across both process and file telemetry so it catches any payload family in the campaign irrespective of filename/packaging. Datadog uses uppercase hex because Sysmon emits @Hashes in uppercase; KQL/Splunk/Falcon use the article's lowercase with case-insensitive matching. Cross-checked against: • https://securelist.com/dozens-of-malicious-wallpapers-found-on-steam-workshop/120186/ • https://www.technadu.com/malicious-steam-workshop-wallpapers-hijack-accounts-via-wallpaper-engine-distribute-darkkomet-lumma-vidar-and-renengine/629591/

  • AV/EDR quarantine copy re-hashed in a watched directory
  • Malware-research VM telemetry inside the monitored estate
  • Hash collision (negligible for MD5 at this scale but theoretically possible)
Response runbook
1) Triage: confirm the matched hash and the host/user; determine whether the file executed or was only written, and identify the parent (wallpaper/loader). 2) Contain: isolate the host, block all 13 hashes org-wide, and reset the affected user's Steam credentials/sessions. 3) Hunt: from each hit pivot to AggregatorHost.dll loads, Synaptics.exe persistence, and C2 to 120.48.156.17 / 202.144.192.29; review Steam Workshop download history on the host.

| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem where Filesystem.file_hash IN ("95856f2ce428c728d9781d3296558068","af080780cca2acd1d082ce01e7cc346a","c133c3dd9f7d6934598025047df41abf","d1693bbff456ae8fa3360446706df6da","8c2cc585ad8a13a72a704c0fda0c9854","b9fa763a53da3eea742d0f3c845a8c09","ded08ae5df7f1b12e5fdb767dbbed0b1","20965254e29104986e11939decd39549","18dedc0009f0927cba6425c84cce9883","0f4f01c6d495abb37403072dd017ce8d","5620f01284329f561b1839a36be55355","fe1f6485013cd5e6d5cf718049b0b8d6","74414ed4b63aadec039b603c32762b80") by Filesystem.dest Filesystem.file_name Filesystem.file_path Filesystem.file_hash | `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)` | `security_content_ctime(firstTime)` | `security_content_ctime(lastTime)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem where Filesystem.file_hash IN ("95856f2ce428c728d9781d3296558068","af080780cca2acd1d082ce01e7cc346a","c133c3dd9f7d6934598025047df41abf","d1693bbff456ae8fa3360446706df6da","8c2cc585ad8a13a72a704c0fda0c9854","b9fa763a53da3eea742d0f3c845a8c09","ded08ae5df7f1b12e5fdb767dbbed0b1","20965254e29104986e11939decd39549","18dedc0009f0927cba6425c84cce9883","0f4f01c6d495abb37403072dd017ce8d","5620f01284329f561b1839a36be55355","fe1f6485013cd5e6d5cf718049b0b8d6","74414ed4b63aadec039b603c32762b80") by Filesystem.dest Filesystem.file_name Filesystem.file_path Filesystem.file_hash | `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)` | `security_content_ctime(firstTime)` | `security_content_ctime(lastTime)`
Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations Command & Control Medium
C2 channel detection via inter-beacon-time stddev / fan-out to single dest.
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1071.004
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where RemoteIPType == "Public" and ActionType == "ConnectionSuccess"
| project DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, Timestamp
| sort by DeviceName asc, RemoteIP asc, RemotePort asc, Timestamp asc
| extend prev_dev = prev(DeviceName, 1), prev_ip = prev(RemoteIP, 1),
         prev_port = prev(RemotePort, 1), prev_ts = prev(Timestamp, 1)
| where DeviceName == prev_dev and RemoteIP == prev_ip and RemotePort == prev_port
| extend delta_sec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, prev_ts)
| summarize conn_count = count(), avg_delta = avg(delta_sec), stdev_delta = stdev(delta_sec)
    by DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| where conn_count > 30 and avg_delta between (30.0 .. 600.0) and stdev_delta < 5.0
| order by conn_count desc
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(2h)
| where DvcAction != "Block"
| where ipv4_is_private(DstIpAddr) == false
| summarize ConnCount = count(),
            DistinctMinutes = dcount(bin(TimeGenerated, 1m))
            by DvcHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber
| where ConnCount > 50 and DistinctMinutes > 30   // sustained, not bursty
| order by ConnCount desc
NETWORK
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.action="allowed" AND All_Traffic.dest_category!="internal"
    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| streamstats current=f last(_time) AS prev_time by src, dest
| eval delta = _time - prev_time
| stats avg(delta) AS avg_delta stdev(delta) AS sd_delta count by src, dest
| where count > 30 AND sd_delta < 5 AND avg_delta>=30 AND avg_delta<=600
| sort - count
| tstats summariesonly=false count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.action="allowed" AND All_Traffic.dest_category!="internal"
    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| streamstats current=f last(_time) AS prev_time by src, dest
| eval delta = _time - prev_time
| stats avg(delta) AS avg_delta stdev(delta) AS sd_delta count by src, dest
| where count > 30 AND sd_delta < 5 AND avg_delta>=30 AND avg_delta<=600
| sort - count
Network connections to article IPs / domains Command & Control High
Outbound traffic to attacker infrastructure named in the article.
ATT&CKT1071
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic Web Network_Resolution.DNS DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where RemoteIP in ("202.144.192.29", "120.48.156.17") or RemoteUrl has_any ("brightly.to")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, RemoteIP, RemotePort, RemoteUrl,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine
let BadIPs     = dynamic(["202.144.192.29", "120.48.156.17"]);
let BadDomains = dynamic(["brightly.to"]);
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where DstIpAddr in (BadIPs)
   or Url has_any (BadDomains)
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber, Url, NetworkProtocol
| order by TimeGenerated desc

title: Outbound Connection to Article-Named IP / Domain
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d0f
status: experimental
description: |
    Replace `__IP_LIST__` / `__DOMAIN_LIST__` placeholders with
    article-specific destinations. For dynamic IOC management, use a
    watchlist or external feed.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/tactics/TA0011/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.command-and-control
logsource:
    category: network_connection
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_ip:
        DestinationIp:
            - '__IP_PLACEHOLDER_1__'
            - '__IP_PLACEHOLDER_2__'
    selection_domain:
        DestinationHostname:
            - '__DOMAIN_PLACEHOLDER_1__'
            - '__DOMAIN_PLACEHOLDER_2__'
    condition: selection_ip or selection_domain
falsepositives:
    - None on a true-positive IOC match
level: critical
NETWORK
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.dest IN ("202.144.192.29", "120.48.156.17")
    by All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest, All_Traffic.dest_port
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| append
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count from datamodel=Web
        where Web.dest IN ("brightly.to")
        by Web.src, Web.dest, Web.url, Web.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`]
| append
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count from datamodel=Network_Resolution.DNS
        where DNS.query IN ("brightly.to")
        by DNS.src, DNS.query, DNS.answer
     | `drop_dm_object_name(DNS)`]
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.dest IN ("202.144.192.29", "120.48.156.17")
    by All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest, All_Traffic.dest_port
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| append
    [| tstats summariesonly=false count from datamodel=Web
        where Web.dest IN ("brightly.to")
        by Web.src, Web.dest, Web.url, Web.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`]
| append
    [| tstats summariesonly=false count from datamodel=Network_Resolution.DNS
        where DNS.query IN ("brightly.to")
        by DNS.src, DNS.query, DNS.answer
     | `drop_dm_object_name(DNS)`]
Infostealer — non-browser process accessing browser cookie/login DBs Actions on Objectives High
Stealers (RedLine, Lumma, Vidar, Atomic) read Login Data / cookies SQLite from Chrome/Edge/Firefox.
ATT&CKT1539 T1555.003
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem DeviceFileEvents
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
| where FolderPath has_any (@"\Google\Chrome\User Data\", @"\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\", @"\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\")
| where FileName in~ ("Login Data","Cookies","logins.json","cookies.sqlite")
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, FolderPath, FileName, ActionType

// ASIM ImFileEvent — covers MDE, Sysmon, AuditD, Defender for Cloud, etc.
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
| where TargetFilePath has_any (@"\Google\Chrome\User Data\",
                                  @"\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\",
                                  @"\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\")
| where TargetFileName in~ ("Login Data","Cookies","logins.json","cookies.sqlite")
| where ActingProcessName !in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName,
          TargetFilePath, TargetFileName, EventType

title: Infostealer - Non-Browser Process Accessing Browser Credential Stores
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d01
status: experimental
description: |
    Stealers (RedLine, Lumma, Vidar, Atomic) read Login Data / cookies
    SQLite databases from Chrome/Edge/Firefox profile directories. Any
    non-browser process touching these files is a high-fidelity signal.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1539/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1555/003/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1539
    - attack.t1555.003
    - attack.credential-access
logsource:
    category: file_access
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_path:
        TargetFilename|contains:
            - '\Google\Chrome\User Data\'
            - '\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\'
            - '\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\'
    selection_file:
        TargetFilename|endswith:
            - '\Login Data'
            - '\Cookies'
            - '\logins.json'
            - '\cookies.sqlite'
    filter_browser:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\chrome.exe'
            - '\msedge.exe'
            - '\firefox.exe'
            - '\brave.exe'
            - '\opera.exe'
    condition: selection_path and selection_file and not filter_browser
falsepositives:
    - Backup utilities reading user profile files
    - Browser sync agents from non-stock vendors
level: high
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where (Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Cookies*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\logins.json*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\cookies.sqlite*")
      AND NOT Filesystem.process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.process_name, Filesystem.file_path, Filesystem.user
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where (Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Cookies*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\logins.json*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\cookies.sqlite*")
      AND NOT Filesystem.process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.process_name, Filesystem.file_path, Filesystem.user
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
Ransomware-style mass file rename / extension change Actions on Objectives Medium
Threshold detection: many files renamed in short window, often with new extension.
ATT&CKT1486
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem DeviceFileEvents
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
| where ActionType in ("FileRenamed","FileModified")
| summarize files = dcount(FileName) by DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, bin(Timestamp, 1m)
| where files > 200    // empirical: > 200 unique-file renames in 1m by one account on one host
                       //            is well above the P99 of legitimate bulk-tooling
| order by files desc

ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
| where EventType in ("FileRenamed","FileModified")
| summarize files = dcount(TargetFileName)
            by DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, bin(TimeGenerated, 1m)
| where files > 200    // P99 of legit bulk-tooling per-minute rename volume
| order by files desc
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count, dc(Filesystem.file_name) AS files
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where Filesystem.action IN ("modified","renamed")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.user, _time span=1m
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| where files > 200
| sort - files
| tstats summariesonly=false count, dc(Filesystem.file_name) AS files
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where Filesystem.action IN ("modified","renamed")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.user, _time span=1m
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| where files > 200
| sort - files
LSASS process access / dump (credential theft) Actions on Objectives High
Mimikatz, comsvcs.dll MiniDump, or any non-Windows process opening LSASS.
ATT&CKT1003.001 T1003
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceEvents
DeviceEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where ActionType == "OpenProcessApiCall"
| where FileName =~ "lsass.exe"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("MsSense.exe","MsMpEng.exe","csrss.exe",
                                          "svchost.exe","wininit.exe","services.exe",
                                          "lsm.exe","SearchProtocolHost.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFolderPath, AccountName
| order by Timestamp desc
// SecurityEvent EventID 4663 = object access. AccessMask 0x10 / 0x40 / 0x1010
// indicate read access to lsass.exe — credential-dump signature. Audit
// Object Access > Audit File System policy required.
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4663
| where ObjectName endswith "\lsass.exe"
| where Account !endswith "$"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, ObjectName, ProcessName,
          AccessMask, AccessReason
| order by TimeGenerated desc

title: LSASS Process Access Outside Microsoft-Signed Tooling
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d04
status: experimental
description: |
    Anything opening lsass.exe with read-memory access that isn't a
    Microsoft signed component (Defender, csrss, etc.) is suspect.
    Mimikatz / Pypykatz / nanodump signature.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1003/001/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1003.001
    - attack.credential-access
logsource:
    category: process_access
    product: windows
detection:
    selection:
        TargetImage|endswith: '\lsass.exe'
    filter_known_good:
        SourceImage|endswith:
            - '\MsSense.exe'
            - '\MsMpEng.exe'
            - '\csrss.exe'
            - '\svchost.exe'
            - '\wininit.exe'
            - '\services.exe'
            - '\lsm.exe'
            - '\SearchProtocolHost.exe'
    condition: selection and not filter_known_good
falsepositives:
    - Third-party EDR / forensic tools — extend the filter list
level: high
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where (Processes.process="*lsass*" OR Processes.process="*sekurlsa*"
        OR Processes.process="*MiniDump*" OR Processes.process="*comsvcs.dll*MiniDump*"
        OR Processes.process="*procdump*lsass*")
       OR (Processes.process_name="rundll32.exe" AND Processes.process="*comsvcs*MiniDump*")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process_name, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where (Processes.process="*lsass*" OR Processes.process="*sekurlsa*"
        OR Processes.process="*MiniDump*" OR Processes.process="*comsvcs.dll*MiniDump*"
        OR Processes.process="*procdump*lsass*")
       OR (Processes.process_name="rundll32.exe" AND Processes.process="*comsvcs*MiniDump*")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process_name, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
Remote service execution — PsExec / SMB lateral movement Actions on Objectives High
psexec / paexec / smbexec / wmic /node — service install over SMB from remote host.
ATT&CKT1021.002 T1569.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceProcessEvents
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where FileName in~ ("psexec.exe","psexesvc.exe","paexec.exe","smbexec.py")
   or (FileName =~ "wmic.exe" and ProcessCommandLine has "/node:")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by Timestamp desc

SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688            // process-create (audit-policy required)
| where Account !endswith "$"
| where NewProcessName endswith "\psexec.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\psexesvc.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\paexec.exe"
   or (NewProcessName endswith "\wmic.exe" and CommandLine has "/node:")
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName, CommandLine,
          ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc

title: PsExec / SMB Lateral Movement Tooling Execution
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d03
status: experimental
description: |
    PsExec, paexec, smbexec, csexec, remcom — admin-grade tooling that
    pivots over SMB. Pair with `wmic /node:` for the full cluster.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1021/002/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1569/002/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1021.002
    - attack.t1569.002
    - attack.lateral-movement
    - attack.execution
logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_psexec:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\psexec.exe'
            - '\psexec64.exe'
            - '\psexesvc.exe'
            - '\paexec.exe'
            - '\csexec.exe'
            - '\remcom.exe'
            - '\smbexec.py'
    selection_wmic_remote:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\wmic.exe'
        CommandLine|contains:
            - '/node:'
    condition: selection_psexec or selection_wmic_remote
falsepositives:
    - Sysadmins running approved remote-management tooling — wrap with
      a known-admin-host watchlist
level: high
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.process_name IN ("psexec.exe","psexesvc.exe","paexec.exe","smbexec.py")
       OR (Processes.process_name="wmic.exe" AND Processes.process="*/node:*")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process_name, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.process_name IN ("psexec.exe","psexesvc.exe","paexec.exe","smbexec.py")
       OR (Processes.process_name="wmic.exe" AND Processes.process="*/node:*")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process_name, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match Installation High
Match SHA256/SHA1/MD5 named in the article against EDR file/process telemetry.
ATT&CKT1027
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem Endpoint.Processes DeviceFileEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Pre-filter each table BEFORE the union — the engine cannot push
// predicates across `union`, and DeviceFileEvents lacks ProcessCommandLine
// (Initiating only) so column-projection has to differ per side.
union
    ( DeviceFileEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("95856f2ce428c728d9781d3296558068", "af080780cca2acd1d082ce01e7cc346a", "c133c3dd9f7d6934598025047df41abf", "d1693bbff456ae8fa3360446706df6da", "8c2cc585ad8a13a72a704c0fda0c9854", "b9fa763a53da3eea742d0f3c845a8c09", "ded08ae5df7f1b12e5fdb767dbbed0b1", "20965254e29104986e11939decd39549", "18dedc0009f0927cba6425c84cce9883", "0f4f01c6d495abb37403072dd017ce8d", "5620f01284329f561b1839a36be55355", "fe1f6485013cd5e6d5cf718049b0b8d6", "74414ed4b63aadec039b603c32762b80") or SHA1 in~ ("95856f2ce428c728d9781d3296558068", "af080780cca2acd1d082ce01e7cc346a", "c133c3dd9f7d6934598025047df41abf", "d1693bbff456ae8fa3360446706df6da", "8c2cc585ad8a13a72a704c0fda0c9854", "b9fa763a53da3eea742d0f3c845a8c09", "ded08ae5df7f1b12e5fdb767dbbed0b1", "20965254e29104986e11939decd39549", "18dedc0009f0927cba6425c84cce9883", "0f4f01c6d495abb37403072dd017ce8d", "5620f01284329f561b1839a36be55355", "fe1f6485013cd5e6d5cf718049b0b8d6", "74414ed4b63aadec039b603c32762b80") or MD5 in~ ("95856f2ce428c728d9781d3296558068", "af080780cca2acd1d082ce01e7cc346a", "c133c3dd9f7d6934598025047df41abf", "d1693bbff456ae8fa3360446706df6da", "8c2cc585ad8a13a72a704c0fda0c9854", "b9fa763a53da3eea742d0f3c845a8c09", "ded08ae5df7f1b12e5fdb767dbbed0b1", "20965254e29104986e11939decd39549", "18dedc0009f0927cba6425c84cce9883", "0f4f01c6d495abb37403072dd017ce8d", "5620f01284329f561b1839a36be55355", "fe1f6485013cd5e6d5cf718049b0b8d6", "74414ed4b63aadec039b603c32762b80")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceFileEvents" ),
    ( DeviceProcessEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where AccountName !endswith "$"

let BadHashes = dynamic(["95856f2ce428c728d9781d3296558068", "af080780cca2acd1d082ce01e7cc346a", "c133c3dd9f7d6934598025047df41abf", "d1693bbff456ae8fa3360446706df6da", "8c2cc585ad8a13a72a704c0fda0c9854", "b9fa763a53da3eea742d0f3c845a8c09", "ded08ae5df7f1b12e5fdb767dbbed0b1", "20965254e29104986e11939decd39549", "18dedc0009f0927cba6425c84cce9883", "0f4f01c6d495abb37403072dd017ce8d", "5620f01284329f561b1839a36be55355", "fe1f6485013cd5e6d5cf718049b0b8d6", "74414ed4b63aadec039b603c32762b80"]);
union
    ( ImFileEvent
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where TargetFileSHA256 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileSHA1 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileMD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType,
                  TargetFileName, TargetFilePath, TargetFileSHA256,
                  Cmd = ActingProcessName, Source = "ImFileEvent" ),

                  TargetFileSHA256 = SHA256,
                  Cmd = TargetProcessCommandLine, Source = "ImProcessCreate" )
| order by TimeGenerated desc

SprySOCKS (FishMonger/I-SOON) C2 beacon to hardcoded Vultr IPs 207.148.78.36 / 207.148.75.122 AICommand & Control Medium
Hunts outbound connections to the two hardcoded SprySOCKS infrastructure IPs ESET attributed to FishMonger: WIN_PLUS C&C 207.148.78.36 (TCP/UDP/WebSocket on 443/53/80) and delivery server 207.148.75.122. These are hard IOCs confirmed by multiple vendors, so any egress to them is high-fidelity regardless of the initiating binary (the WIN_DRV variant diverts C2 over a random TCP port, so do not pin on a fixed listening port). Rationale: Uses the two ESET-published hardcoded IPs (207.148.78.36 C&C and 207.148.75.122 delivery server), each confirmed by Security Affairs and gbhackers. Matching on exact IP rather than the broader shared Vultr /20 keeps FP near zero. Cross-checked against: • https://www.welivesecurity.com/en/eset-research/fishmongers-arsenal-upgraded-sprysocks-windows/ • https://securityaffairs.com/193728/apt/china-linked-fishmonger-ports-sprysocks-to-windows-with-kernel-level-stealth-and-uefi-bootkit-hints.html • https://gbhackers.com/sprysocks-windows-backdoor-uses-kernel/
ATT&CKT1071 T1095 T1571
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • A different, benign tenant workload legitimately rents the same recycled Vultr IP after the campaign infrastructure was torn down (Vultr IPs are reassigned)
  • Security researcher / sandbox detonation host in your environment deliberately contacting the IOC
  • Threat-intel enrichment tooling or IOC-validation scanner probing the address
  • NAT/proxy egress IP making the source attribution ambiguous (confirm the real internal host)
Response runbook
1) Triage: identify the internal host and the InitiatingProcessFileName/SHA1 making the connection; pull the process tree and check whether the binary SHA1 matches the SprySOCKS hash list (UC2). 2) Contain: network-isolate the host, block 207.148.78.36, 207.148.75.122 and review the wider 207.148.64.0/20 Vultr range at the perimeter; preserve memory for the kernel-driver rootkit. 3) Hunt: pivot on the host for unsigned/hidden kernel driver loads, hidden listening ports, EFI System Partition tampering (UC3), and any other host beaconing to the same /20.

| where RemoteIP in ("207.148.78.36", "207.148.75.122")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessFolderPath, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, RemoteIP, RemotePort, Protocol, InitiatingProcessSHA1
| order by Timestamp desc
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where DstIpAddr in ("207.148.78.36", "207.148.75.122")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, SrcIpAddr, SrcUsername, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber, NetworkProtocol, NetworkApplicationProtocol, DstHostname
| order by TimeGenerated desc

SprySOCKS WIN_DRV/WIN_PLUS backdoor binary by ESET SHA1 hash AIInstallation Medium
Detects execution, file write, or image load of any of the 11 SprySOCKS Windows binaries (WIN_DRV / WIN_PLUS variants and loaders) by their ESET-published SHA1 hashes. WIN_DRV ships a kernel driver that hides its own processes, files, registry keys and network connections, so on-host hash matching at write/load time is the most reliable surface before the rootkit engages. Rationale: All 11 SHA1 values are the ESET-published SprySOCKS sample hashes from the article IOC block, cross-checked against the ESET blog mirror and Security Affairs. Hash matching is exact and survives the rootkit's process/file hiding because it fires at write/load time. Cross-checked against: • https://www.welivesecurity.com/en/eset-research/fishmongers-arsenal-upgraded-sprysocks-windows/ • https://www.esetngblog.com/post/fishmonger-s-arsenal-upgraded-sprysocks-for-windows • https://securityaffairs.com/193728/apt/china-linked-fishmonger-ports-sprysocks-to-windows-with-kernel-level-stealth-and-uefi-bootkit-hints.html
ATT&CKT1014 T1543.003
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes Endpoint.Filesystem
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • AV/EDR quarantine copies or VirusTotal-uploaded sample handling on an analyst/sandbox host re-surfacing the same hash
  • Threat-intel platform storing the sample on disk during enrichment
  • Re-used hash from a generic packer producing a benign-file collision (extremely unlikely for SHA1, but verify file path/signer)
  • Purple-team or detection-validation exercise intentionally dropping the IOC
Response runbook
1) Triage: confirm the hit is on a production endpoint (not a sandbox/IR jump box); capture FolderPath, signer, and the InitiatingProcess that wrote/loaded it. 2) Contain: isolate the host immediately, collect a memory image before the kernel driver can re-hide artifacts, and submit the binary for analysis. 3) Hunt: search the org for any of the other 10 hashes, for connections to the UC1 C2 IPs, for service installations and EFI/boot tampering (UC3), and scope FishMonger lateral movement to other government/high-value hosts.

SprySOCKS WIN_DRV BlackLotus-style Secure Boot downgrade / EFI bootkit (CVE-2023-24932) AIInstallation Low
Hunts for the UEFI bootkit component ESET reports as a 'limited indication' in some SprySOCKS attacks: a CVE-2023-24932 BlackLotus-style downgrade that writes a revoked/older boot manager (bootmgfw.efi/bootmgr.efi/bootx64.efi) onto the EFI System Partition. Flags .efi writes to boot paths by processes other than the Windows servicing stack — the EDR-blind firmware persistence this campaign may layer on top of the kernel rootkit. Rationale: Targets the article's CVE-2023-24932 UEFI bootkit lead by detecting the BlackLotus-style core action — writing a (revoked/downgraded) boot manager to the EFI System Partition — excluding the Windows servicing stack that legitimately updates these files. Confidence is Low because ESET itself frames the bootkit as a 'limited indication'. Cross-checked against: • https://www.welivesecurity.com/en/eset-research/fishmongers-arsenal-upgraded-sprysocks-windows/ • https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/topic/how-to-manage-the-windows-boot-manager-revocations-for-secure-boot-changes-associated-with-cve-2023-24932-41a975df-beb2-40c1-99a3-b3ff139f832d • https://www.huntress.com/threat-library/vulnerabilities/cve-2023-24932
ATT&CKT1542.003 T1553.006
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Legitimate Windows cumulative/feature update or KB5025885 Secure Boot servicing applying the boot manager (TrustedInstaller/TiWorker — filtered, but third-party servicing tools may not be)
  • OEM/IT imaging and BCD repair via bcdboot.exe / dism during provisioning
  • BitLocker recovery or bootrec /rebuildbcd troubleshooting by a sysadmin
  • Endpoint backup/restore agents touching the ESP
  • Dual-boot or Linux bootloader (e.g. shim/grub) installation writing .efi files
Suppression filter
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("bcdboot.exe","dism.exe","setuphost.exe","reagentc.exe") and not (InitiatingProcessFolderPath has @"\Windows\WinSxS\")
Response runbook
1) Triage: identify the writing process and its signer; confirm whether it is a sanctioned servicing/imaging tool and whether the dropped .efi is Microsoft-signed and current (compare hash/version against a known-good). 2) Contain: if non-servicing, isolate the host, verify Secure Boot state and DBX revocation status, and treat as firmware-level compromise — reimage may be insufficient; rebuild the ESP from trusted media. 3) Hunt: correlate the host with UC1 C2 beacons and UC2 SprySOCKS hashes, review for Memory Integrity/HVCI or BitLocker being disabled, unrecognized .efi files, BCD edits, and apply CVE-2023-24932 DBX revocations fleet-wide.
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where FileName endswith ".efi"
| where FileName in~ ("bootmgfw.efi","bootmgr.efi","bootx64.efi") or FolderPath has @"\EFI\" or FolderPath has "HarddiskVolume"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("TiWorker.exe","TrustedInstaller.exe","poqexec.exe","MoUsoCoreWorker.exe","CompatTelRunner.exe","wuauclt.exe","setup.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA1, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessFolderPath, InitiatingProcessCommandLine
| order by Timestamp desc
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where TargetFileName endswith ".efi"
| where TargetFileName in~ ("bootmgfw.efi","bootmgr.efi","bootx64.efi") or TargetFilePath has @"\EFI\" or TargetFilePath has "HarddiskVolume"
| where ActingProcessName !has "TrustedInstaller.exe" and ActingProcessName !has "TiWorker.exe" and ActingProcessName !has "poqexec.exe" and ActingProcessName !has "CompatTelRunner.exe"
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, DvcAction, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, TargetFilePath, TargetFileName, TargetFileSHA1
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: Boot Manager EFI Write to EFI System Partition (CVE-2023-24932 Bootkit Downgrade)
id: 9d4a1f72-08be-4c63-bb15-7a2e6c0f9b31
description: Detects writes of bootmgfw.efi/bootmgr.efi/bootx64.efi to the EFI System Partition by a non-servicing process, consistent with a CVE-2023-24932 BlackLotus-style downgrade observed alongside SprySOCKS WIN_DRV.
references:
  - https://www.welivesecurity.com/en/eset-research/fishmongers-arsenal-upgraded-sprysocks-windows/
  - https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/topic/how-to-manage-the-windows-boot-manager-revocations-for-secure-boot-changes-associated-with-cve-2023-24932-41a975df-beb2-40c1-99a3-b3ff139f832d

date: 2026/06/20

logsource:

detection:
  selection:
    TargetFilename|endswith:
      - '\bootmgfw.efi'
      - '\bootmgr.efi'
      - '\bootx64.efi'
  filter_servicing:
    Image|endswith:
      - '\TrustedInstaller.exe'
      - '\TiWorker.exe'
      - '\poqexec.exe'
      - '\CompatTelRunner.exe'
  condition: selection and not filter_servicing
level: high
source:windows.sysmon @EventID:11 @TargetFilename:(*\\bootmgfw.efi OR *\\bootmgr.efi OR *\\bootx64.efi OR *\\EFI\\* OR *\\bootmgfw.EFI OR *\\BOOTMGFW.EFI) -@Image:(*\\TrustedInstaller.exe OR *\\TiWorker.exe OR *\\poqexec.exe OR *\\CompatTelRunner.exe)
#event_simpleName=FileWritten
| TargetFileName=/\\(bootmgfw|bootmgr|bootx64)\.efi$/i
| NOT (ContextImageFileName=/\\(TrustedInstaller|TiWorker|poqexec|CompatTelRunner|wuauclt)\.exe$/i)

Asset exposure — vulnerability matches article CVE(s) Reconnaissance High
Match vulnerability scanner output to the CVE(s) named in the article.
ATT&CKT1190
Data sourcesVulnerabilities DeviceInfo DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
// TVM tables are daily snapshots — pin a 1-day window so the engine
// partitions on Timestamp instead of scanning the full retention.
DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where CveId in~ ("CVE-2023-24932")
| join kind=inner (DeviceInfo | where Timestamp > ago(1d)) on DeviceId
| project DeviceName, OSPlatform, CveId, VulnerabilitySeverityLevel, RecommendedSecurityUpdate
| order by VulnerabilitySeverityLevel asc, DeviceName asc

// Sentinel has no native TVM table. If MDE→Sentinel streaming is enabled,
// `DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities` is available. Otherwise this UC has
// no Sentinel translation — track via Update / Heartbeat OS-version
// gaps as a coarse approximation.
DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| where CveId in~ ("CVE-2023-24932")
| join kind=inner (DeviceInfo | where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)) on DeviceId
| project DeviceName, OSPlatform, CveId,
          VulnerabilitySeverityLevel, RecommendedSecurityUpdate
| order by VulnerabilitySeverityLevel asc, DeviceName asc

// Pre-filter both ASIM tables before the union — same pattern as the
// Defender version so the engine can push hash predicates per-side.
let BadHashes = dynamic(["955BFC3DCC867256F9F46A606DEB0779FA3416D8", "44DC4A08C5EB0972C8E18B0E01284E06F09006BB", "AB87B29B6F79487C75CA08D102E79001E536F083", "6490B8E4AADE25A3EE2DA9A47F312DB2122470BC", "E7484C24B88A1A2407A8F09D734F9A993670285B", "621D1952839BE4B0A1B0E66E87BCE5062CA368ED", "2457EED2AB28E37741F10914EF929DAD2C8079D4", "D2C706B1EAF662BF0CE124B5032F73ED84BDA24A", "5F3B87CEF56683D9A9E19186E0FD0D8019B559C4", "C793CA31E3F6628B5C8986146953BF66232E9A30", "037DB2445F3D72388CB2CF8510563148E5A184BE"]);
union
    ( ImFileEvent
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where TargetFileSHA256 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileSHA1 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileMD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType,
                  TargetFileName, TargetFilePath, TargetFileSHA256,
                  Cmd = ActingProcessName, Source = "ImFileEvent" ),
    ( ImProcessCreate
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ (BadHashes) or SHA1 in~ (BadHashes) or MD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileName = TargetProcessName, TargetFilePath = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileSHA256 = SHA256,
                  Cmd = TargetProcessCommandLine, Source = "ImProcessCreate" )
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Actions on Objectives
Detected
Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration.
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad). → [LLM] Fake Microsoft account security-alert spear-phish delivering ZIP-with-LNK (APT37/ScarCruft) · [LLM] NarwhalRAT LNK-spawned batch downloader fetching payload + CAT file from APT37 C2 · Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution · Email attachment opened from external sender
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → Office app spawning script/LOLBin child process · Fake CAPTCHA / clipboard-injected PowerShell (ClickFix / FakeCaptcha) · PowerShell encoded / obfuscated command
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key. → [LLM] NarwhalRAT scheduled-task persistence by exact task name (MicrosoftUserInterfacePicturesUpdateTackMachine) · Scheduled task created with suspicious image / encoded args · File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking. → [LLM] NarwhalRAT C2 to APT37 Korean relay domains/IPs · [LLM] NarwhalRAT pCloud dead-drop resolver secondary C2 from Python loader · Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations · Network connections to article IPs / domains
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage. → [LLM] NarwhalRAT 'naverwhale' staging directory under %APPDATA% · Infostealer — non-browser process accessing browser cookie/login DBs
Fake Microsoft account security-alert spear-phish delivering ZIP-with-LNK (APT37/ScarCruft) AIDelivery Medium
Hunts inbound email impersonating a Microsoft Account security/OTP alert from a non-Microsoft sender domain that carries a ZIP attachment (the NarwhalRAT delivery vector observed by Genians). The article's lure is a fake 'abnormal OTP activity' notice whose attachment is a ZIP containing a malicious LNK rather than the promised HWP advisory. Rationale: Anchors on the article's exact lure (fake MS account/OTP security alert) + the specific delivery shape (inbound ZIP attachment from a non-Microsoft sender domain). Sentinel left empty: this tenant's Sentinel schema has no native O365 email/attachment table (EmailEvents is Defender XDR only); detect via Defender AH instead. Cross-checked against: • https://www.genians.co.kr/en/blog/threat_intelligence/narwhalrat • https://gbhackers.com/apt37-hackers-use-narwhalrat-malware/ • https://cybersecuritynews.com/powershell-and-python-loader-to-deploy-narwhalrat/
ATT&CKT1566.001 T1656
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Legitimate breach/credential-alert digests from third-party password managers or identity providers using 'security alert' subjects
  • Internal phishing-simulation campaigns spoofing Microsoft branding
  • Partner/vendor sending genuine .zip with 'security' in the subject (audit reports, SBOMs)
  • Marketing newsletters from security vendors with Microsoft in the display name
Suppression filter
| where AuthenticationDetails has_any ("spf:fail","dmarc:fail","compauth:fail","spf:softfail")
Response runbook
1) Triage: detonate/examine the ZIP in a sandbox — confirm it contains a .lnk (not the promised HWP). Check SPF/DKIM/DMARC alignment in AuthenticationDetails and whether SenderDisplayName spoofs Microsoft over a mismatched domain. 2) Contain: purge the message tenant-wide (soft-delete + block sender domain/IP), and check UrlClickEvents/DeviceFileEvents for any recipient who already extracted or ran the LNK. 3) Hunt: on any host that opened the attachment, pivot to UC2-UC6 — schtasks named MicrosoftUserInterfacePicturesUpdateTackMachine, %APPDATA%\naverwhale, and connections to daehoat.com / novel21.co.kr.

NarwhalRAT LNK-spawned batch downloader fetching payload + CAT file from APT37 C2 AIDelivery High
Detects the multi-stage loader where a launched LNK drives cmd/PowerShell/LOLBin downloaders to retrieve the obfuscated batch script, Python binary and Windows security catalog (CAT) file from APT37 C2 hosts. Fires on a download utility whose command line references the named C2 domains or pulls a .cat over HTTP. Rationale: Pins the article's loader stage on the five corroborated C2 domains appearing in a LOLBin command line, plus the distinctive '.cat over HTTP' fetch — both are high-fidelity, low-FP because legitimate software does not download a security catalog from these Korean relay hosts. Cross-checked against: • https://www.genians.co.kr/en/blog/threat_intelligence/narwhalrat • https://cybersecuritynews.com/powershell-and-python-loader-to-deploy-narwhalrat/
ATT&CKT1204.002 T1059.003 T1105
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Internal admin script that happens to fetch a legitimately-hosted .cat catalog over HTTP for driver signing
  • Security researcher manually curling one of the C2 domains during analysis on a sandbox/host with telemetry
  • Web-content filter test scripts referencing flagged domains in command lines
  • PowerShell deployment tooling using DownloadFile to a benign internal mirror that an analyst mis-tunes the domain list against
Response runbook
1) Triage: pull the full process tree — confirm the parent is explorer.exe (LNK launch) or a batch under cmd.exe, and resolve which C2 domain/.cat was fetched. 2) Contain: isolate the host, block the five C2 domains at proxy/DNS, and quarantine the downloaded python binary + CAT file. 3) Hunt: check the same host for the scheduled task names (UC3), %APPDATA%\naverwhale (UC4), and outbound C2/pCloud beacons (UC5/UC6); sweep the org for the same parent-LNK pattern.
let LookbackDays = 14d;
let C2Domains = dynamic(["daehoat.com","novel21.co.kr","fe01.co.kr","webhostingkorea.com","crwellfood.com"]);
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where FileName in~ ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","curl.exe","certutil.exe","bitsadmin.exe","mshta.exe")
| where ProcessCommandLine has_any (C2Domains)
   or (ProcessCommandLine has ".cat" and ProcessCommandLine has_any ("http://","https://","DownloadFile","DownloadString","-urlcache","Start-BitsTransfer","Invoke-WebRequest"))
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("explorer.exe","cmd.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","powershell.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, ParentProcess = InitiatingProcessFileName, ParentCmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
let C2Domains = dynamic(["daehoat.com","novel21.co.kr","fe01.co.kr","webhostingkorea.com","crwellfood.com"]);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(14d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where NewProcessName has_any ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","curl.exe","certutil.exe","bitsadmin.exe","mshta.exe")
| where CommandLine has_any (C2Domains)
   or (CommandLine has ".cat" and CommandLine has_any ("http://","https://","DownloadFile","-urlcache","Start-BitsTransfer","Invoke-WebRequest"))
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("explorer.exe","cmd.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","powershell.exe")
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName, CommandLine, ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: NarwhalRAT Loader Downloader Contacting APT37 C2 Domains
id: 3b71e2c4-5d18-4f6a-9c0b-1e7a2d9f4c63
status: experimental
description: Detects a Windows command shell or download LOLBin whose command line references APT37/ScarCruft NarwhalRAT C2 domains during the multi-stage LNK loader chain.
references:
  - https://thehackernews.com/2026/06/fake-microsoft-alerts-used-to-deploy.html
  - https://www.genians.co.kr/en/blog/threat_intelligence/narwhalrat
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/06/20
tags:
  - attack.t1105
  - attack.t1059.003
  - attack.command_and_control
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: windows
detection:
  selection:
    Image|endswith:
      - '\cmd.exe'
      - '\powershell.exe'
      - '\pwsh.exe'
      - '\curl.exe'
      - '\certutil.exe'
      - '\bitsadmin.exe'
      - '\mshta.exe'
    CommandLine|contains:
      - 'daehoat.com'
      - 'novel21.co.kr'
      - 'fe01.co.kr'
      - 'webhostingkorea.com'
      - 'crwellfood.com'
  condition: selection
level: high
source:windows.sysmon @EventID:1 @Image:(*\cmd.exe OR *\powershell.exe OR *\curl.exe OR *\certutil.exe OR *\bitsadmin.exe OR *\mshta.exe OR *\CMD.EXE OR *\PowerShell.exe) @CommandLine:(*daehoat.com* OR *novel21.co.kr* OR *fe01.co.kr* OR *webhostingkorea.com* OR *crwellfood.com*)
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2 ImageFileName=/(cmd|powershell|pwsh|curl|certutil|bitsadmin|mshta)\.exe$/i
| ParentBaseFileName=/(explorer|cmd|wscript|cscript|powershell)\.exe$/i
| CommandLine=/(daehoat\.com|novel21\.co\.kr|fe01\.co\.kr|webhostingkorea\.com|crwellfood\.com)/i
| table([_time, aid, ComputerName, UserName, ParentBaseFileName, ImageFileName, CommandLine])
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where (Processes.process_name IN ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","curl.exe","certutil.exe","bitsadmin.exe","mshta.exe")) (Processes.process="*daehoat.com*" OR Processes.process="*novel21.co.kr*" OR Processes.process="*fe01.co.kr*" OR Processes.process="*webhostingkorea.com*" OR Processes.process="*crwellfood.com*") by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.parent_process_name Processes.process_name Processes.process
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime)
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where (Processes.process_name IN ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","curl.exe","certutil.exe","bitsadmin.exe","mshta.exe")) (Processes.process="*daehoat.com*" OR Processes.process="*novel21.co.kr*" OR Processes.process="*fe01.co.kr*" OR Processes.process="*webhostingkorea.com*" OR Processes.process="*crwellfood.com*") by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.parent_process_name Processes.process_name Processes.process
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime)
NarwhalRAT scheduled-task persistence by exact task name (MicrosoftUserInterfacePicturesUpdateTackMachine) AIInstallation High
Detects creation of the uniquely-named scheduled tasks APT37 uses to persist NarwhalRAT and its sibling Python chain. The names 'MicrosoftUserInterfacePicturesUpdateTackMachine' and 'MicrosoftMusicLibrariesPackageTaskMachine' are attacker-specific masquerades and have no legitimate use. Rationale: The two task names are verbatim, attacker-coined strings from the article (note the deliberate 'Tack'/'Task' typo) with zero legitimate footprint — effectively a behavioural hash, making this near-zero-FP alerting. Cross-checked against: • https://www.genians.co.kr/en/blog/threat_intelligence/narwhalrat • https://gbhackers.com/apt37-hackers-use-narwhalrat-malware/
ATT&CKT1053.005
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Threat-hunt or detection-validation exercise that re-creates the named task in a lab
  • Red-team emulation of APT37 reusing the published task name
  • Backup/restore of a previously-compromised system image re-registering the task
Response runbook
1) Triage: dump the task's action (schtasks /query /tn <name> /xml) — confirm it launches the CAT/Python in-memory chain, and identify the user context. 2) Contain: delete the task (schtasks /delete), isolate the host, and capture the CAT file + %APPDATA%\naverwhale contents before remediation. 3) Hunt: sweep the fleet for both task names and for the loader (UC2) and C2 (UC5/UC6); review who received the fake MS alert email (UC1).
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where ProcessCommandLine has_any ("MicrosoftUserInterfacePicturesUpdateTackMachine","MicrosoftMusicLibrariesPackageTaskMachine")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where EventID in (4698, 4688)
| where (EventID == 4698 and (EventData has "MicrosoftUserInterfacePicturesUpdateTackMachine" or EventData has "MicrosoftMusicLibrariesPackageTaskMachine"))
   or (EventID == 4688 and NewProcessName endswith "schtasks.exe" and (CommandLine has "MicrosoftUserInterfacePicturesUpdateTackMachine" or CommandLine has "MicrosoftMusicLibrariesPackageTaskMachine"))
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, SubjectUserName, Account, EventID, NewProcessName, CommandLine, EventData
| order by TimeGenerated desc

NarwhalRAT 'naverwhale' staging directory under %APPDATA% AIActions on Objectives High
Detects file activity in the %APPDATA%\naverwhale directory NarwhalRAT uses to stage harvested data (keystrokes, screenshots, audio, USB and directory dumps). The folder name masquerades as Naver Whale browser and is the malware's namesake. Rationale: The literal staging path %APPDATA%\naverwhale is the malware's named artifact (the 'NarwhalRAT' moniker derives from it) and has no legitimate Naver Whale equivalent in Roaming — a single-string, high-confidence host indicator. Cross-checked against: • https://www.genians.co.kr/en/blog/threat_intelligence/narwhalrat • https://gbhackers.com/apt37-hackers-use-narwhalrat-malware/
ATT&CKT1074.001 T1036.005
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Genuine Naver Whale browser writing profile data (its real path is under \AppData\Local\Naver\Naver Whale, not \Roaming\naverwhale — so true overlap is rare)
  • Analyst/IR tooling copying a captured sample's folder onto a telemetry-monitored workstation
  • Backup software indexing a previously-infected user profile
Suppression filter
| where not (FolderPath has @"\AppData\Local\Naver\Naver Whale")
Response runbook
1) Triage: enumerate naverwhale folder contents and the InitiatingProcess writing to it (expect python.exe / pythonw.exe), and confirm path is under \Roaming (not the legit \Local\Naver\Naver Whale). 2) Contain: isolate the host, preserve the directory for forensics (it holds staged keystroke/screenshot/audio data), then remove the scheduled task and payload. 3) Hunt: correlate the writing process to outbound C2 (UC5) and pCloud exfil (UC6); scope which data types were staged to gauge exposure.
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where FolderPath has @"\AppData\Roaming\naverwhale" or FolderPath has @"\naverwhale\"
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine
| order by Timestamp desc
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where TargetFilePath has @"\AppData\Roaming\naverwhale" or TargetFilePath has "naverwhale"
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, EventType, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, TargetFilePath, TargetFileName
| order by TimeGenerated desc

NarwhalRAT C2 to APT37 Korean relay domains/IPs AICommand & Control Medium
Detects host connections to the corroborated NarwhalRAT primary C2 relays (daehoat.com, novel21.co.kr and four sibling domains plus six C2 IPs). These Korean-hosted relays are the malware's main command channel per Genians. Rationale: Uses the six C2 IPs and five domains corroborated across Genians/gbhackers; matching them in network/DNS telemetry is a direct IOC hit with negligible FP outside of intentional analyst lookups. Cross-checked against: • https://www.genians.co.kr/en/blog/threat_intelligence/narwhalrat • https://gbhackers.com/apt37-hackers-use-narwhalrat-malware/
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1105
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • SOC/TI analyst manually browsing or sandbox-detonating against the listed domains from a monitored host
  • Proxy/IDS signature-test traffic deliberately generated to these IOCs
  • Stale IOC: one of the Korean relays gets reclaimed/parked and reused by a benign site (re-validate domains periodically)
  • Threat-intel feed connector pre-fetching the domains for enrichment
Response runbook
1) Triage: identify the InitiatingProcess making the connection (expect python.exe/pythonw.exe staging from %APPDATA%\naverwhale) and the volume/cadence of beacons. 2) Contain: block all five domains and six IPs at perimeter/DNS, isolate any beaconing host. 3) Hunt: pivot from each hitting host to the loader (UC2), scheduled task (UC3) and naverwhale staging (UC4); check for the secondary pCloud dead-drop channel (UC6) in case primary C2 is blocked.
let C2Domains = dynamic(["daehoat.com","novel21.co.kr","fe01.co.kr","webhostingkorea.com","crwellfood.com"]);
let C2IPs = dynamic(["121.254.222.10","121.254.222.80","211.239.157.126","218.150.78.198","218.150.78.231","61.100.9.206"]);
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where RemoteUrl has_any (C2Domains) or RemoteIP in (C2IPs)
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessFolderPath, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, RemoteUrl, RemoteIP, RemotePort, ActionType
| order by Timestamp desc
let C2Domains = dynamic(["daehoat.com","novel21.co.kr","fe01.co.kr","webhostingkorea.com","crwellfood.com"]);
let C2IPs = dynamic(["121.254.222.10","121.254.222.80","211.239.157.126","218.150.78.198","218.150.78.231","61.100.9.206"]);
union
  (DnsEvents | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d) | where Name has_any (C2Domains) | project TimeGenerated, Computer, ClientIP, Indicator = Name, Kind = "dns"),
  (ImNetworkSession | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d) | where DstIpAddr in (C2IPs) or Url has_any (C2Domains) | project TimeGenerated, Computer = DvcHostname, ClientIP = SrcIpAddr, Indicator = coalesce(Url, DstIpAddr), Kind = "conn")
| order by TimeGenerated desc

NarwhalRAT pCloud dead-drop resolver secondary C2 from Python loader AICommand & Control Medium
Hunts the malware's secondary C2 channel: a non-browser Python process reaching pCloud cloud-storage endpoints, used as a dead-drop resolver (the code processes pCloud 'folderid'/'auth' parameters). Correlated to hosts that also show the naverwhale staging directory to cut benign pCloud usage. Rationale: Targets the article's named secondary channel — Python (the NarwhalRAT runtime) abusing the pCloud API as a dead-drop resolver. Host-scoping the Defender/Sentinel variants to machines with the naverwhale artifact suppresses the bulk of legitimate pCloud-client traffic; the EDR variants additionally require python.exe (not the pCloud desktop client) as the initiator. Cross-checked against: • https://www.genians.co.kr/en/blog/threat_intelligence/narwhalrat • https://cybersecuritynews.com/powershell-and-python-loader-to-deploy-narwhalrat/
ATT&CKT1102.001 T1071.001
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Legitimate pCloud desktop sync client or browser uploading user files (excluded here by requiring python.exe initiator / naverwhale host)
  • A data-science workstation running python scripts that legitimately call the pCloud API
  • Developer using a pcloud Python SDK for backups
  • CI/automation agent built on Python pushing artifacts to pCloud
Suppression filter
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("pcloud.exe","pclouddrive.exe","msedge.exe","chrome.exe","firefox.exe")
Response runbook
1) Triage: confirm the initiating binary is python.exe/pythonw.exe (not pcloud.exe) and that the host carries %APPDATA%\naverwhale; capture the URL/folderid if visible in proxy logs. 2) Contain: isolate the host, block pcloud.com egress for that asset, and revoke/rotate any credentials that may have been staged. 3) Hunt: tie the Python process back to the scheduled-task chain (UC3) and primary C2 (UC5); review whether exfil to pCloud succeeded by sizing outbound bytes, and sweep other naverwhale hosts for the same pCloud pattern.
let NaverwhaleHosts = DeviceFileEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(30d)
    | where FolderPath has "naverwhale"
    | distinct DeviceId;
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where RemoteUrl has "pcloud.com"
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("python.exe","pythonw.exe") or InitiatingProcessFolderPath has @"\AppData\" or DeviceId in (NaverwhaleHosts)
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessFolderPath, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, RemoteUrl, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| order by Timestamp desc
let NaverwhaleHosts = ImFileEvent
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
    | where TargetFilePath has "naverwhale"
    | distinct DvcHostname;
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where Url has "pcloud.com" or DstHostname has "pcloud.com"
| where DvcHostname in (NaverwhaleHosts)
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, SrcUsername, SrcIpAddr, Url, DstHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber
| order by TimeGenerated desc
source:windows.sysmon @EventID:3 @Image:(*\python.exe OR *\pythonw.exe OR *\Python.exe OR *\PYTHON.EXE) @DestinationHostname:(*pcloud.com* OR *Pcloud.com*)
#event_simpleName=DnsRequest DomainName=/pcloud\.com/i ContextImageFileName=/python(w)?\.exe$/i
| table([_time, aid, ComputerName, DomainName, ContextImageFileName, ContextProcessId])

| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime)
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic where All_Traffic.dest_host="*pcloud.com*" (All_Traffic.app="python.exe" OR All_Traffic.app="pythonw.exe" OR All_Traffic.process_name="python.exe" OR All_Traffic.process_name="pythonw.exe") by All_Traffic.src All_Traffic.dest_host All_Traffic.dest_port All_Traffic.app
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime)
Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations Command & Control Medium
C2 channel detection via inter-beacon-time stddev / fan-out to single dest.
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1071.004
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where RemoteIPType == "Public" and ActionType == "ConnectionSuccess"
| project DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, Timestamp
| sort by DeviceName asc, RemoteIP asc, RemotePort asc, Timestamp asc
| extend prev_dev = prev(DeviceName, 1), prev_ip = prev(RemoteIP, 1),
         prev_port = prev(RemotePort, 1), prev_ts = prev(Timestamp, 1)
| where DeviceName == prev_dev and RemoteIP == prev_ip and RemotePort == prev_port
| extend delta_sec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, prev_ts)
| summarize conn_count = count(), avg_delta = avg(delta_sec), stdev_delta = stdev(delta_sec)
    by DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| where conn_count > 30 and avg_delta between (30.0 .. 600.0) and stdev_delta < 5.0
| order by conn_count desc
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(2h)
| where DvcAction != "Block"
| where ipv4_is_private(DstIpAddr) == false
| summarize ConnCount = count(),
            DistinctMinutes = dcount(bin(TimeGenerated, 1m))
            by DvcHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber
| where ConnCount > 50 and DistinctMinutes > 30   // sustained, not bursty
| order by ConnCount desc
NETWORK
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.action="allowed" AND All_Traffic.dest_category!="internal"
    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| streamstats current=f last(_time) AS prev_time by src, dest
| eval delta = _time - prev_time
| stats avg(delta) AS avg_delta stdev(delta) AS sd_delta count by src, dest
| where count > 30 AND sd_delta < 5 AND avg_delta>=30 AND avg_delta<=600
| sort - count
| tstats summariesonly=false count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.action="allowed" AND All_Traffic.dest_category!="internal"
    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| streamstats current=f last(_time) AS prev_time by src, dest
| eval delta = _time - prev_time
| stats avg(delta) AS avg_delta stdev(delta) AS sd_delta count by src, dest
| where count > 30 AND sd_delta < 5 AND avg_delta>=30 AND avg_delta<=600
| sort - count
Network connections to article IPs / domains Command & Control High
Outbound traffic to attacker infrastructure named in the article.
ATT&CKT1071
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic Web Network_Resolution.DNS DeviceNetworkEvents

let BadIPs     = dynamic(["121.254.222.10", "121.254.222.80", "211.239.157.126", "218.150.78.198", "218.150.78.231", "61.100.9.206"]);

| where Timestamp > ago(7d)

description: |

    SQLite databases from Chrome/Edge/Firefox profile directories. Any
    non-browser process touching these files is a high-fidelity signal.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1539/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1555/003/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:

    - attack.t1555.003
    - attack.credential-access
logsource:
    category: file_access
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_path:
        TargetFilename|contains:
            - '\Google\Chrome\User Data\'
            - '\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\'
            - '\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\'
    selection_file:
        TargetFilename|endswith:
            - '\Login Data'
            - '\Cookies'
            - '\logins.json'
            - '\cookies.sqlite'
    filter_browser:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\chrome.exe'
            - '\msedge.exe'
            - '\firefox.exe'
            - '\brave.exe'
            - '\opera.exe'
    condition: selection_path and selection_file and not filter_browser
falsepositives:
    - Backup utilities reading user profile files
    - Browser sync agents from non-stock vendors
level: high
